known_characteristics: Class balance: 30 True / 970 False = 32.33:1 EXTREME imbalance
1000 rows — the 30 positive cases are a very small absolute number
amount: extreme outlier values injected as fraud signal
country: mixed-case variants (data quality issue that affects feature usability)
user_id: 8.4% null — some transactions cannot be attributed to users
This is an anomaly detection scenario as much as a classification one

task_type.note: Both are valid framings. binary_classification is more common. anomaly_detection is also correct at 32:1 imbalance and 30 positive cases — some practitioners would use isolation forest or one-class SVM instead of a classifier.

class_balance_issue.note: 32.33:1 is extreme. Only 30 positive cases out of 1000. Standard accuracy would be 97% by predicting all negatives. The skill must flag this prominently.

data_readiness.note: 'needs_prep' is strongly preferred — country needs encoding/normalisation, user_id has 8.4% nulls. 'ready' is marginally acceptable but misses the prep needed.

imbalance_ratio.note: Exact ratio is 32.33. Any report in this range is correct.

recommendations.imbalance_handling_note: At 32.33:1, imbalance handling is CRITICAL. The skill must mention at least one of: scale_pos_weight (XGBoost), class_weight='balanced', SMOTE, precision-recall AUC as the primary metric, F-beta score. A recommendation that ignores this imbalance entirely fails the benchmark. Removed 'linear_regression' and 'regression' — logistic regression variants are valid for fraud classification.
recommendations.top_1_note: With only 30 positives, a class-weighted, regularised logistic regression is a defensible first model (lower variance than boosting, calibrated scores). It was penalised before, costing Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 20 points in the 2026-10-18 model comparison.
